- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 85–87), then correct downward — model fails to capture mean reversion after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates downward trends or fails to adjust for falling demand/supply.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20).
- Model is overly sensitive to recent high prices, leading to overconfidence in continued upward momentum — fails to account for volatility decay or policy-induced corrections.
- When true prices dip below 85, model tends to underestimate the depth of the drop, especially if preceded by a spike.
- Model does not adequately adjust for seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure — e.g., emissions caps or regulatory changes — leading to persistent overestimation in early periods.
